arxiv-1905-07756.title: The classification of complex algebraic surfaces
arxiv-1905-07756.creator: Ciro Ciliberto
arxiv-1905-07756.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Ciro Ciliberto. These notes contain the classification of complex algebraic surfaces following Mori’s theory. They includes the P 12 P_{12} –Theorem, Sarkisov’s programme in the surface case and Noether–Castelnuovo’s Theorem in its classical version. Introduction This text grew up from the notes of a graduate course I gave at the University of Roma “Tor Vergata” in the academic year 2018–19. The subject is the classification of complex algebraic surfaces following Mori’s theory.

arxiv-1912-01387.title: Pricing FX Options under Intermediate Currency
arxiv-1912-01387.creator: S. Maurer, T.E. Sharp, M.V. Tretyakov
arxiv-1912-01387.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by S. Maurer, T.E. Sharp, M.V. Tretyakov. We suggest an intermediate currency approach that allows us to price options on all FX markets simultaneously under the same risk-neutral measure which ensures consistency of FX option prices across all markets. In particular, it is sufficient to calibrate a model to the volatility smile on the domestic market as, due to the consistency of pricing formulas, the model automatically reproduces the correct smile for the inverse pair (the foreign market).

arxiv-2105-00965.title: Timescales of the chaos onset in the general relativistic Poynting-Robertson effect
arxiv-2105-00965.creator: Vittorio De Falco 1, William Borrelli 2
arxiv-2105-00965.description: Abstract It has been proved that the general relativistic Poynting-Robertson effect in the equatorial plane of Kerr metric shows a chaotic behavior for a suitable range of parameters. As a further step, we calculate the timescale for the onset of chaos through the Lyapunov exponents, estimating how this trend impacts on the observational dynamics.

arxiv-2311-04634.title: VET: Visual Error Tomography for Point Cloud Completion and High-Quality Neural Rendering Journal: TOG Conference: SIGGRAPH Asia 2023 Conference Papers; December 12–15, 2023; Sydney, NSW, Australia DOI: 10.1145/3610548.3618212 CCS: Computing methodologies Rendering CCS: Computing methodologies Image
arxiv-2311-04634.creator: Linus Franke, Darius Rückert, Laura Fink, Matthias Innmann, Marc Stamminger
arxiv-2311-04634.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Linus Franke, Darius Rückert, Laura Fink, Matthias Innmann, Marc Stamminger. In the last few years, deep neural networks opened the doors for big advances in novel view synthesis. Many of these approaches are based on a (coarse) proxy geometry obtained by structure from motion algorithms. Small deficiencies in this proxy can be fixed by neural rendering, but larger holes or missing parts, as they commonly appear for thin structures or for glossy regions, still lead to distracting artifacts and temporal instability.

arxiv-2510-14184.title: MAFA: A Multi-Agent Framework for Enterprise-Scale Annotation with Configurable Task Adaptation
arxiv-2510-14184.creator: Mahmood Hegazy, Aaron Rodrigues, Azzam Naeem
arxiv-2510-14184.description: Abstract We present MAFA (Multi-Agent Framework for Annotation), a production-deployed system that transforms enterprise-scale annotation workflows through configurable multi-agent collaboration. Addressing the critical challenge of annotation backlogs in financial services, where millions of customer utterances require accurate categorization, MAFA combines specialized agents with structured reasoning and a judge-based consensus mechanism.

arxiv-2510-25526.title: Non-bulging Baker domains for transcendental skew products Thanks: This material is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant No. 1440140, while the first and third authors were in residence at the Mathematical Sciences Research Institute in Berkeley, California, durin
arxiv-2510-25526.creator: Anna Miriam Benini, Tom Potthink, Jasmin Raissy
arxiv-2510-25526.description: Abstract . In this paper we show that Baker domains of transcendental skew products can either bulge or not, depending on the higher order terms. This is in contrast to polynomial skew products where all Fatou components with bounded orbits of an invariant attracting fiber do bulge. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 37F80; Secondary 30D05, 32H50, 37F10 1.

arxiv-2601-08005.title: Internal Deployment Gaps in AI Regulation
arxiv-2601-08005.creator: Joe Kwon, Stephen Casper
arxiv-2601-08005.description: Abstract . Frontier AI regulations primarily focus on systems deployed to external users, where deployment is more visible and subject to outside scrutiny. However, high-stakes applications can occur internally when companies deploy highly capable systems within their own organizations, such as for automating R&D, accelerating critical business processes, and handling sensitive proprietary data.

pmc-11465644.title: Chemical Exposomics in Human Plasma by Lipid Removal and Large-Volume Injection Gas Chromatography–High-Resolution Mass Spectrometry
pmc-11465644.creator: Hongyu Xie, Kalliroi Sdougkou, Bénilde Bonnefille, Stefano Papazian, Ingvar A Bergdahl, Panu Rantakokko, Jonathan W Martin
pmc-11465644.description: For comprehensive chemical exposomics in blood, analytical workflows are evolving through advances in sample preparation and instrumental methods. We hypothesized that gas chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (GC-HRMS) workflows could be enhanced by minimizing lipid coextractives, thereby enabling larger injection volumes and lower matrix interference for improved target sensitivity and nontarget molecular discovery.

pmc-11595697.title: The Effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy on Insomnia Severity Among Menopausal Women: A Scoping Review
pmc-11595697.creator: Anastasia Ntikoudi, Dimitra Anna Owens, Alketa Spyrou, Eleni Evangelou, Eugenia Vlachou, Luca Steardo
pmc-11595697.description: This review explores the impact of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) on menopausal women suffering from insomnia. The transition to menopause is often accompanies by sleep disturbances, which significantly affect women’s quality of life. This review applies a scoping approach to evaluate randomized controlled trials (RCTs) focused on CBT-I interventions for insomnia among menopausal women.

pmc-11678020.title: Development of Green Fluorescent Protein-Tagged Strains of Fusarium acuminatum via PEG-Mediated Genetic Transformation
pmc-11678020.creator: Fangyi Ju, Zhongqiang Qi, Jiajin Tan, Tingting Dai
pmc-11678020.description: Fusarium acuminatum is recognized as the causative agent of root rot in many forestry and agricultural plants. In recent years, root rot and foliage blight caused by F. acuminatum have become widespread and severe in China, particularly affecting Dianthus chinensis. The infection mechanism of F. acuminatum remains a pressing area for research.

pmc-11689961.title: CROSS-CULTURE ADAPTATION AND VALIDATION OF THE CHINESE VERSION OF MANCHESTER COPD FATIGUE SCALE (MCFS)
pmc-11689961.creator: Haihong Zhang, Chongmei Huang, Minhui Liu
pmc-11689961.description: Fatigue is an aching, complex, and multifaceted sensation that is the second most prominent and disabling symptom of COPD, approximately 50% of COPD patients suffer from severe fatigue. Various scales or questionnaires has been developed to measure fatigue in COPD patients.

pmc-12464183.title: The improved features to dose correlation for dose volumes prediction in multidisease radiation therapy plans
pmc-12464183.creator: Peng Zhou, Jia Luo, Honghao Xu, Shengxiu Jiao, Chuan Chen
pmc-12464183.description: Determining whether input features are consistently strongly correlated with organ-at-risk (OAR) dose across different diseases can improve the accuracy of dose-volume histogram (DVH) prediction in knowledge-based treatment planning. In this study, we utilized patient geometric and dosimetric data to establish correlations with OAR doses and investigated the differences between distance-to-dose and dosimetric-to-dose relationships.

pmc-12555720.title: Investigating the Risk Factors in Progression of HIV Disease Using an Illness-Death Multistate Model
pmc-12555720.creator: Roghayyeh Hassanzadeh, Hossein Mahjub, Mohammad Mirzaei, Fariba Keramat, Maryam Farhadian
pmc-12555720.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: The trend of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease progress is different for every patient. Some patients may experience events during the course of their disease that can affect disease progression and death. The main objective of the present study was to investigate the effect of risk factors in progression of HIV disease, taking into account intermediate events, using a multistate model.Study Design: A retrospective cohort study.

pmc-12613334.title: Top three priorities for artificial intelligence integration into emergency, critical, and perioperative medicine: an interdisciplinary clinical expert consensus
pmc-12613334.creator: Beatrice Loriga, Francesco Baglivo, Valentina Bellini, Chiara Adembri, Jonathan Montomoli, Marco Cascella, Giacomo Diedenhofen, Luigi De Angelis, Nicola Gentili, Mattia Altini, Antonio Pastori, Raffaella Gaggeri, Elena Giovanna Bignami
pmc-12613334.description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied in emergency, critical, and perioperative medicine, yet its implementation remains limited and fragmented. Variability in digital maturity, governance, and clinical readiness continues to challenge large-scale adoption.MethodsA multidisciplinary expert consensus was conducted to identify key priorities for the safe and effective integration of AI in high-acuity settings.

pmc-12788221.title: The Impact of the Accelerometer Sampling Rate on the Performance of Machine and Deep Learning Models in Wearable Fall-Detection Systems
pmc-12788221.creator: Manny Villa, Eduardo Casilari
pmc-12788221.description: Population aging has intensified the prevalence of falls among older adults, making automatic Fall Detection Systems (FDS) a key component of telemonitoring and remote care. Among wearable-based approaches, inertial sensors, particularly accelerometers, offer an effective and low-cost alternative for continuous monitoring. However, the impact of the selection of the sampling frequency on model performance remains insufficiently explored.

pmc-13205141.title: Cranial Base Morphology and Mandibular Growth in Skeletal Deep Bite: A Longitudinal Study in Prepubertal Children
pmc-13205141.creator: Eugen Silviu Bud, Mariana Păcurar, Cristina Ioana Bica, Sorana Maria Bucur, Alexandru Vlasa, Beáta Szabó, Anamaria Bud
pmc-13205141.description: Background: Skeletal deep bite malocclusion (Angle Class II division 2) represents a common vertical skeletal discrepancy characterized by excessive anterior overbite and a hypodivergent craniofacial growth pattern. The contribution of cranial base morphology to mandibular growth direction during early development remains incompletely understood.

pmc-13584437.title: Implementation and evaluation of an insulin use manual in the public health system of a Peruvian Region: a mixed-methods study
pmc-13584437.creator: Cecilia Anza-Ramirez, Karen Bonilla-Aguilar, Joaquín Carrasco-Zavala, José A Diaz-RG, Janeth Tenorio-Mucha, Jessica Hanae Zafra-Tanaka, Dulce Moran, Jessica Faustor Sanchez, Angela Guillermina Roncal Vergara, Maria Lazo-Porras
pmc-13584437.description: BackgroundDiabetes is a major public health issue, especially in low-and middle- income countries (LMICs) where barriers to care are common. Despite insulin’s critical role, access remains limited due to market concentration, weak policies, poor availability, and lack of trained staff.

pmc-13644212.title: A characterized promoter suite enables metabolic rewiring of the acetogen Acetobacterium woodii toward ethanol production
pmc-13644212.creator: Renaud Eynard, Sephora Justine, Rémi Hocq, Stefan Pflügl
pmc-13644212.description: Acetogenic bacteria are promising platforms for converting gaseous and liquid one-carbon (C1) substrates such as carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide (CO2), formate and methanol into fuels and chemicals, but their application is limited by sparse genetic tools and poor control over metabolic fluxes.

pmc-13674291.title: C-Reactive Protein and Risk of Low Back Pain: A Univariable and Multivariable Mendelian Randomization Study
pmc-13674291.creator: Shalin Feng, Jun Mou, Xiaoqin Wang, Changping Mu
pmc-13674291.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the causal associations of genetically predicted C-reactive protein (CRP), major depressive disorder (MDD), body mass index (BMI), and smoking initiation with low back pain (LBP) using Mendelian randomization (MR).MethodsSummary-level GWAS data for exposures and LBP (FinnGen R8) were obtained. Instrumental variables were selected at a strict genome-wide threshold (P < 5×10−8) and harmonized.

uslaw-usc-t51-s70505.title: 51 U.S.C. § 70505 — Lunar outpost
uslaw-usc-t51-s70505.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t51-s70505.description: United States Code, Title 51 (National And Commercial Space Programs); Chapter 705 (Exploration Initiatives). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Establishment.— As the Administration works toward the establishment of a lunar outpost, the Administration shall make no plans that would require a lunar outpost to be occupied to maintain its viability. Any such outpost shall be operable as a human-tended facility capable.
